content: Illness, also referred to as ill-health, is defined as a state of poor health. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), health is described as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity. When these conditions are not met, an individual is considered to be ill or experiencing an illness. The fields of medicine and pharmacology aim to treat or alleviate the symptoms of illnesses or medical conditions. The term developmental disability refers to severe, lifelong disabilities caused by mental and/or physical impairments. Abnormal conditions affecting the body or mind that result in discomfort, dysfunction, or distress for the individual or those around them are classified as illnesses. In some contexts, the term illness is used broadly to encompass injuries, disabilities, syndromes, infections, symptoms, deviant behaviors, and atypical variations in structure or function. In other contexts, these may be categorized separately. A pathogen, or infectious agent, is a biological entity that causes disease or illness in its host. A passenger virus is a virus that resides in or infects the body without causing symptoms, illness, or disease. Foodborne illnesses, commonly referred to as food poisoning, occur when food contaminated with pathogenic bacteria, toxins, viruses, prions, or parasites is consumed. Mental illness, also known as emotional disability or cognitive dysfunction, is a broad term encompassing conditions that may involve emotional instability, behavioral dysregulation, or cognitive impairment. Specific mental illnesses include major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Mental illnesses can have biological origins, such as anatomical, chemical, or genetic factors, or psychological origins, such as trauma or conflict. These conditions can impair an individual's ability to work, attend school, or maintain healthy relationships. Other terms for mental illness include mental disorder, psychiatric disorder, psychological disorder, abnormal psychology, emotional disability, emotional problems, or behavioral problems. The term insanity is used in legal contexts rather than medical ones. Brain damage can result from a variety of conditions, illnesses, or injuries. A delusion is defined as a fixed, false belief that is pathological in nature, often resulting from an illness or disease process. Munchausen syndrome is a condition in which an individual fabricates, exaggerates, or induces symptoms of illness in themselves to gain attention, treatment, or sympathy. Munchausen syndrome by proxy involves inducing illness in another person for similar reasons. The term mental health consumer refers to individuals receiving treatment for psychiatric illnesses or disorders. This term was introduced to empower individuals with mental health conditions, emphasizing their role in choosing their treatment and highlighting their importance in the mental health care system. Social determinants of health refer to the social conditions in which individuals live, which significantly influence their health. Illnesses are often linked to social, economic, political, and environmental factors. Organizations such as the Public Health Agency of Canada and the World Health Organization recognize the profound impact of social determinants on both individual and collective well-being. Government involvement is crucial in studying various illnesses and treatments. Health care encompasses the prevention, treatment, and management of illnesses, as well as the preservation of mental and physical well-being, through services provided by medical, nursing, and allied health professionals. The organized delivery of these services constitutes a health care system. Historically, the term healthcare was not commonly used; instead, people referred to medicine or the health sector and discussed the treatment and prevention of illnesses and diseases. A patient is any individual receiving medical attention, care, or treatment, typically due to illness or injury. The term health consumer or health care consumer is also used to describe patients, particularly by governmental agencies, insurance companies, or patient advocacy groups. Medical emergencies are conditions or injuries that pose an immediate threat to an individual's health or life, requiring urgent medical attention. Emergency medicine is a specialized field focused on managing medical emergencies and resuscitating patients. Emergency departments provide initial care for a wide range of illnesses and injuries, some of which may be life-threatening and require immediate intervention. A drug is any chemical substance, excluding food or devices, that affects the function of living organisms. Drugs can be used therapeutically to treat illnesses or recreationally to alter behavior and perception. Medications, typically produced by pharmaceutical companies, are often patented, while non-patented versions are referred to as generic drugs. Physicians may prescribe medications for purposes other than their approved indications, a practice known as off-label use. Drug marketing materials specify the illnesses or medical conditions for which the drug has been proven safe and effective. A drug overdose occurs when a substance is consumed in quantities or concentrations that disrupt the body's homeostasis, potentially causing severe illness or death. In biological terms, poisons are substances capable of causing illness. Bedrest is a medical treatment involving prolonged periods of lying down, either in a hospital or at home, to aid recovery. While most hospitalized patients spend significant time in bed, the term bedrest typically refers to extended periods of rest at home. Human enhancement technologies (HET) are tools designed not only to treat illnesses and disabilities but also to enhance human abilities and characteristics. Medications are licensed drugs used to treat or alleviate symptoms of illnesses or medical conditions. A wheelchair is a mobility device designed for individuals who cannot walk due to illness or disability. Shock therapy involves the controlled induction of a physiological state of shock for psychiatric treatment purposes. Electrotherapy uses electrical energy to treat health impairments or abnormal conditions. Epidemiology is the scientific study of factors influencing the health and illnesses of individuals and populations. It serves as the foundation for public health interventions and preventive medicine. Behavioral medicine is an interdisciplinary field that integrates psychosocial, behavioral, and biomedical knowledge relevant to health and illness. The Clinical Global Impression (CGI) scale is used to assess treatment responses in patients with mental disorders. Its Improvement scale requires clinicians to evaluate how much a patient's illness has improved or worsened compared to their baseline state. Mental confusion and decreased alertness may indicate a worsening of a chronic illness.
